value.body: Trust and safety analysts decide whether content, ads or accounts on an online platform break its rules or the law. They are hired by social media, marketplace and gaming platforms and by outsourcing firms that run review teams for them. A typical day is a queue of flagged cases, judgement calls on grey areas, and escalation of serious ones.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Any graduate degree; humanities degrees are common

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Internal review queues, policy guidelines, spreadsheets

items.label: Languages
items.value: Regional-language skills are often needed for Indian content

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join a review or moderation team through campus or walk-in hiring and are trained on the platform's policies. Clear written English, reasoning about rules and their exceptions, and one or more Indian languages help. Moving into policy, quality or investigations roles comes with experience.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Applying written rules to unclear cases
Careful reading and attention to detail
Basic knowledge of Indian IT and data laws

value.title: At a glance
items: Some queues involve disturbing material; ask about wellbeing support and rotation.
Shift and weekend work is common.
Next steps: quality analyst, policy specialist, investigations or team lead.
